seo.title: San Francisco Homeless Help - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified shelter, meals, hygiene, health care, benefits, jobs, legal help and other homelessness services in San Francisco.

page.heading: San Francisco homeless help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, fire, overdose or medical emergency: 911 City information and non-emergency street outreach: 311; outside San Francisco call 415-701-2311 SF Homeless Outreach Team and adult shelter line: 628-652-8000 Mental health or substance-use crisis: call or text 988 Behavioral Health Access Line: 888-246-3333, 24 hours
page.notice: Information and capacity can change without notice. Call ahead when possible. A listing does not guarantee a bed, meal, appointment, benefit, job, storage space or housing. Shelter and housing assessments are not promises of placement.
page.footer: See something wrong? Report incorrect information on GitHub. — https://github.com/carlosbranco/no-home-help/issues/new?template=incorrect-information.md

entries.title: Emergency services — 911
entries.description:
Call 911 for immediate danger, serious injury, trouble breathing, unconsciousness, fire, suspected overdose or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location first. If naloxone is available during a suspected opioid overdose, use it and still call 911 because its effect can wear off.
San Francisco coordinated street-response guidance

entries.title: 311 city services
entries.description:
Inside San Francisco: 311. Outside the city: 415-701-2311. TTY: 711.
Available 24 hours a day in more than 160 languages. Use 311 for non-emergency information, service referrals and a request for outreach to a person living outside. Use 911 when someone is in immediate danger.
Official 311 information

entries.title: SF Homeless Outreach Team and Adult Shelter Access Line
entries.description:
Phone: 628-652-8000
Request street outreach, ask about adult shelter access, or register for the adult shelter reservation waitlist. An outreach request or waitlist registration does not reserve a bed. For the waitlist, use either the phone or the online form, not both.
Official 2026 shelter-access guidance

entries.title: 988 and Behavioral Health Access Line
entries.description:
Call or text 988 for suicide, mental-health or substance-use crisis support. For public behavioral-health assessment and treatment navigation, call 888-246-3333, select a language and extension 2. The access line operates 24 hours.
San Francisco treatment navigation guide

entries.title: Adult shelter reservation waitlist
entries.description:
Know the difference: a shelter waitlist is for a temporary bed. Coordinated Entry assesses possible housing and problem-solving resources. Neither process guarantees placement.
Phone: 628-652-8000
For self-sufficient adults age 18 or older without minor children seeking a bed at Next Door, MSC South or Sanctuary. Register once by phone or through the official form. Keep the waitlist identifier and check the list regularly. Registration is not a same-day bed guarantee.
Official 2026 instructions and form link

entries.title: Dolores Shelter Program — walk-up overnight shelter
entries.description:
Published hours: overnight, 6 p.m.–8 a.m.; the first-come line may begin at 5:30 p.m.
Walk-up option for adults without minor children. Capacity is limited and lining up does not guarantee entry. Confirm the current intake process before making a long trip.
Official shelter-access guidance
entries.address: Address: 1050 South Van Ness Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94110

entries.title: MSC South
entries.description:
Phone: 415-597-7960
Adult shelter with meals, showers, case management and support. Access is through the adult shelter reservation system, 311 or SFHOT; it is not a guaranteed walk-in bed.
St. Vincent de Paul official program page
entries.address: Address: 525 Fifth Street, San Francisco, CA 94107

entries.title: Adult Coordinated Entry — ECS Access Point
entries.description:
Phone: 628-626-1386. Drop-in: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 9 a.m.–noon and 12:30–3:45 p.m.; Wednesday, 9 a.m.–noon and 2–3:45 p.m.
For adults age 18 or older without minor children. Offers housing assessment and problem-solving. Assessment may not lead to a housing referral.
Official 2026 access-point table
entries.address: Address: 123 10th Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: Adult Coordinated Entry — Mission Action
entries.description:
Phone: 415-857-7762. Drop-in: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–3:15 p.m.
For adults age 18 or older without minor children. Ask for a housing assessment and problem-solving conversation. Bring documents if available, but call or visit even if papers are missing.
Official 2026 access-point table
entries.address: Address: 2645 Mission Street, San Francisco, CA 94110

entries.title: Adult Coordinated Entry — justice-involved adults
entries.description:
Phone: 415-522-7592. Drop-in: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–3:45 p.m.
Housing access point for justice-involved adults age 18 or older without minor children. An assessment identifies possible next steps but does not guarantee housing.
Official 2026 access-point table
entries.address: Pretrial Diversion Project: 1200 Folsom Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: Family Coordinated Entry — three access points
entries.description:
For households with a minor child and for pregnant people. Call first to confirm hours:
- Central City, Compass: 37 Grove Street; 415-644-0151.
- Mission, Catholic Charities: 2871 Mission Street; 415-972-1281.
- Bayview, Catholic Charities: 1641 La Salle Avenue; 415-430-6320.
Access points provide problem-solving, assessment and navigation. They do not guarantee immediate shelter or permanent housing.
SFUSD family and youth housing resources

entries.title: Immediate family-shelter contacts
entries.description:
- Stay Over Program: 415-879-9095, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; 415-879-4316, 5:30 p.m.–7:30 a.m.
- Compass urgent accommodation: 415-340-0572.
- Oasis Family Shelter: 415-875-9124.
- Queen of Peace Shelter: 415-550-2465.
Call before traveling. Eligibility, intake and spaces change, and a call does not reserve a room.
Current SFUSD family-resource page

entries.title: Lark-Inn — shelter for ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 800-447-8223. Open 24 hours; walk-ins are listed as available.
Nightly bed availability is limited. Young people should arrive by 9:45 p.m. The shelter provides meals, showers, laundry, lockers and a pet kennel. A listing does not guarantee a bed.
Lark-Inn official page
entries.address: Address: 869 Ellis Street, San Francisco, CA 94109

entries.title: Taimon Booton Navigation Center
entries.description:
Shelter and services for transgender, gender-nonconforming and intersex people, and cisgender women. The site is not open to public walk-ins and its address is not published.
For assessment and referral, go to Adult Coordinated Entry at 123 10th Street. Referral and capacity are not guaranteed.
Official program and access instructions

entries.title: Urgent accommodation for survivors of violence
entries.description:
St. Vincent de Paul: 415-940-2864 or 415-940-2866.
Ask about short-term urgent accommodation for an adult fleeing intimate-partner violence, sexual assault or human trafficking while homeless. Eligibility and room availability must be confirmed.
Official 2026 community guidance

entries.title: Veterans Coordinated Entry — Swords to Plowshares
entries.description:
Housing line: 415-727-8387. Drop-in: Monday, 9 a.m.–3:45 p.m.; Tuesday–Friday, 8 a.m.–3:45 p.m.
For veterans age 18 or older without minor children. Staff can assess housing needs and help obtain service documents. Off-site housing does not accept direct walk-ins.
Official 2026 access-point table
entries.address: Address: 1060 Howard Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

categories.title: Free meals, groceries and faith-based help

entries.title: GLIDE Daily Free Meals
entries.description:
Meals: breakfast daily 7:30–9 a.m.; lunch 11:30 a.m.–1 p.m.; dinner 3:30–5 p.m. The first half-hour of breakfast is reserved for seniors, families and adults with disabilities.
No eligibility screening or intake is required. GLIDE is rooted in a church community; worship is not listed as a meal requirement.
GLIDE official meal schedule
entries.address: Address: 330 Ellis Street, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: St. Anthony's Dining Room
entries.description:
Open seven days: breakfast begins at 7 a.m.; lunch is 10 a.m.–1:30 p.m.; a weekday hot meal to go begins at 2 p.m.
Franciscan Catholic organization serving the public. Worship is not listed as a requirement.
Official dining-room page
entries.address: Address: 121 Golden Gate Avenue, first floor, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: Martin de Porres House of Hospitality
entries.description:
Phone: 415-552-0240. Free lunch: Monday–Saturday, noon–2 p.m.
Volunteer-run Catholic Worker community. All are welcome and help is offered without conditions. Meals are often vegetarian and frequently vegan.
Official hours and services
entries.address: Address: 225 Potrero Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: Bayview Drop-In Center and Mother Brown's Kitchen
entries.description:
Phone: 415-671-1100. Breakfast: daily 7–9 a.m. Dinner: weekdays 5–7 p.m.; weekends 4–6 p.m.
No proof of income or outside referral is required, but a general program intake is used. Meals are to go.
Felton Institute official page
entries.address: Address: 2111 Jennings Street, San Francisco, CA 94124

entries.title: San Francisco-Marin Food Bank pantry locator
entries.description:
Use the live locator or call 211 to find free weekly groceries, emergency food and older-adult food boxes. The Food Bank does not distribute directly to the public at its warehouses.
Sites have different registration and pickup rules. Call before traveling and bring bags if possible.
Official pantry network and locator

entries.title: SFHSA free-food directory
entries.description:
The Human Services Agency publishes meal and grocery partners across the city and advises calling each site to confirm hours and availability.
Official San Francisco free-food directory

categories.title: Showers, laundry, clothing, toilets, mail and internet

entries.title: St. Anthony's Hygiene Hub
entries.description:
Free showers, toilets, laundry, hygiene supplies and basic-needs help. Sign-up begins at 6 a.m. and demand can exceed daily capacity. Check the official page or call 415-241-2600 for the current schedule.
Official Hygiene Hub page
entries.address: Address: 150 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: Bayview Drop-In Center — 24-hour facility
entries.description:
Phone: 415-671-1100. Showers and laundry are published daily 8 a.m.–midnight, with last shower at 11:30 p.m. and last wash at 11 p.m. Lockers, rest space and weekday mail service are also available.
A general intake is required. Cleaning closures and availability can affect access.
Current official service hours
entries.address: Address: 2111 Jennings Street, San Francisco, CA 94124

entries.title: Mission Neighborhood Resource Center
entries.description:
Phone: 415-869-7977. Drop-in space, showers, laundry, lockers, restrooms, charging, case management and a clinic. Service windows and women-only periods vary; call before traveling.
Current SF Service Guide listing
entries.address: Address: 165 Capp Street, San Francisco, CA 94110

entries.title: Martin de Porres showers and clothing
entries.description:
Showers: Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–1 p.m., first come. Clothing: Thursdays. Phone: 415-552-0240.
Official current service schedule
entries.address: Address: 225 Potrero Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: St. Anthony's Free Clothing Program
entries.description:
Adults and families with self-determined need may use the program, but an appointment is required. New or returning-after-one-year guests register in person on the first floor. No appointments are made by phone or email.
Official registration and hours
entries.address: Address: 121 Golden Gate Avenue, second floor, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: St. Anthony's Tenderloin Tech Lab
entries.description:
Phone: 415-592-2766. Free computers, internet, printing, scanning, faxing, secure charging, classes and tutoring for adults 18 or older.
No ID is required, but a short annual orientation is. Check the program page for current hours.
Official Tech Lab page
entries.address: Address: 150 Golden Gate Avenue, third floor, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: San Francisco Public Library
entries.description:
Phone: 415-557-4400. Libraries provide indoor public space, restrooms, internet and computer access under library rules. Check the live directory for hours, closures and a closer branch.
Official library locations and hours
entries.address: Main Library: 100 Larkin Street, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: Public bathrooms and drinking-water map
entries.description:
The City publishes a live map of public bathrooms and water fountains. Hours, closures and accessibility vary by location.
Official DataSF map

entries.title: Project Homeless Connect — mail and practical support
entries.description:
Resource line: 855-588-7968. Published on-site hours: Tuesday, 9:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m.; check the calendar for more days.
Offers mail service, referrals, identification help, some health connections and donated items. Appointments, eligibility and stock vary.
Every Day Connect official page
entries.address: Address: 1031 Franklin Street, second floor, entrance at Franklin and O'Farrell, San Francisco, CA 94109

entries.title: Sixth Street Storage and other lockers
entries.description:
The City-funded program remains contracted through 2029, but enrollment, hours and available bins can change. Call 311 or ask an access point before taking belongings there. Bayview Drop-In and Mission Neighborhood Resource Center also list lockers, subject to intake and capacity.
Official storage-program contract
entries.address: Sixth Street Storage: 74 Sixth Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

categories.title: Medical, mental health and substance-use care

entries.title: Tom Waddell Urban Health Clinic
entries.description:
Phone: 415-355-7500. Focuses on adults experiencing homelessness, supportive-housing residents and Tenderloin residents; walk-ins are welcome.
Official clinic flyer
entries.address: Address: 230 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102
entries.hours: Hours: Monday–Wednesday and Friday, 8 a.m.–noon and 1–5 p.m.; Thursday, 1–5 p.m.; closed weekends and City holidays.

entries.title: Street Outreach Services medical van
entries.description:
Dispatch: 415-355-2250
Free urgent and preventive care for unhoused San Franciscans, with connections to primary care. The schedule includes roving sites and can change. Call for the exact location.
Official mobile-clinic schedule

entries.title: Shelter Health
entries.description:
City shelter guests can ask staff for on-site health care, including urgent and wound care, vaccines, medication support, testing and connections to mental-health or substance-use care. This program serves guests at participating shelters; it is not a public walk-in clinic.
Official Shelter Health information

entries.title: Behavioral Health Access Center
entries.description:
Phone: 628-754-9100. Drop-in: weekdays 8 a.m.–7 p.m.; weekends 9 a.m.–4 p.m.
Mental-health assessment and referral for San Francisco residents eligible for Medi-Cal. For 24-hour navigation, call 888-246-3333.
Official 2026 treatment guide
entries.address: Address: 1380 Howard Street, first floor, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: Hospitality House Community Building Program
entries.description:
Phone: 415-329-2005. Drop-in mental-health stabilization and short-term counseling. The City guide lists Monday 2–10 p.m. and Tuesday–Friday 9 a.m.–10 p.m.
Official 2026 treatment guide
entries.address: Address: 169 Sixth Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: Harm Reduction Center
entries.description:
Safer-use supplies, naloxone, syringe disposal, overdose-prevention support, drug checking on selected days, testing and links to care. The latest City schedule found lists Tuesday–Friday 11 a.m.–7 p.m.; confirm before traveling.
Call 911 for a suspected overdose, even after giving naloxone.
Official harm-reduction schedule
entries.address: Address: 117 Sixth Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: CalFresh food benefits
entries.description:
Phone: 855-355-5757. Apply online, by phone or at an SFHSA center. A person experiencing homelessness does not need a household address to start.
If income and money are very low, ask for Expedited Services, which may provide eligible applicants benefits within three business days. People without stable mail or phone may ask about EBT-card pickup.
Official CalFresh application instructions

entries.title: County Adult Assistance Programs — CAAP
entries.description:
Phone: 833-879-1365. Apply through BenefitsCal or in person at 1460 Mission Street.
County cash-assistance programs for eligible low-income adults without dependent children. Ask about shelter connected to the application process; neither cash aid nor shelter is automatic.
Official CAAP page

entries.title: CalWORKs for families with children
entries.description:
Phone: 855-557-5100. Apply online or visit 170 Otis Street or 3120 Mission Street.
Tell the worker immediately if the family urgently needs housing, food, clothing, rent, utilities or medical help; emergency help depends on eligibility.
Official 2026 application steps

entries.title: Medi-Cal health coverage
entries.description:
Phone: 855-355-5757. Apply through BenefitsCal, by phone or at an SFHSA center. Low-income California residents may qualify regardless of age or immigration status, but eligibility review is required.
Official Medi-Cal information

entries.title: SFHSA service centers and mobile service
entries.description:
In-person benefits help is available at 1460 Mission Street, 1440 Harrison Street, 3120 Mission Street, 170 Otis Street and 2 Gough Street for older adults and people with disabilities. Confirm hours before traveling.
Important: 1235 Mission Street is permanently closed. The Mobile Benefits Center calendar offers additional temporary locations and can issue EBT cards when appropriate.
- Official relocation notice
- Mobile Benefits Center calendar — https://www.sfhsa.org/services/mobile-benefits-center

entries.title: Free Muni Access Pass
entries.description:
A 12-month Muni-only pass for eligible people experiencing homelessness in San Francisco. Applicants must have contacted a Coordinated Entry Access Point within the previous six months. It does not cover BART.
Apply online, by mail, or at the SFMTA Customer Service Center, 11 South Van Ness Avenue, weekdays 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
Official SFMTA discounts and Access Pass

entries.title: Centralized Job Center of San Francisco
entries.description:
Free Goodwill career services may include planning, training, hiring events, job boards, and use of computers, phones and fax. Enrollment requirements vary by program.
Official Goodwill career-center page
entries.address: Address: 750 Post Street, San Francisco, CA 94109
entries.hours: Hours: Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., walk-in or appointment; orientations Tuesday and Thursday at 11 a.m.

entries.title: Specialized Job Center for justice-involved adults
entries.description:
Phone: 415-489-7300. Hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m., walk-in or appointment.
Career services and training within the Community Assessment and Services Center for people facing re-entry barriers.
Official career-services page
entries.address: Address: 564 Sixth Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: JobsNOW!
entries.description:
Phone: 877-562-1669
Free SFHSA job matching, paid opportunities, training, résumé, application and interview help. Eligibility generally requires authorization to work and current SFHSA benefits such as CalWORKs, CalFresh or CAAP.
Official JobsNOW! page

entries.title: 3120 Mission Street Employment Information Center
entries.description: Official service-center page
entries.address: Address: 3120 Mission Street, San Francisco, CA 94110
entries.hours: Hours: Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Benefits service center with JobsNOW! connections plus computers, printing, copying and fax for job search.

entries.title: Larkin Street employment and education — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 415-673-0911. Youth support includes employment, education, GED, college, computers and case management. Walk-in navigation is Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–noon; appointments 1–4 p.m.
Official youth drop-in services
entries.address: Address: 134 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: Applying without a home address
entries.description:
Use an authorized mail program rather than an address that has not agreed to receive mail. Project Homeless Connect offers mail service, and Bayview Drop-In lists weekday mail service. The St. Anthony Tech Lab provides free computers, printing, scanning, fax and charging.
Never pay someone who promises a job or asks for money for an application.

entries.title: Project Homeless Connect — identification help
entries.description:
Resource line: 855-588-7968. Eligible participants may receive a no-fee California ID voucher and help seeking birth certificates or passports. Help depends on eligibility, appointments and funds.
Official identification and mail services
entries.address: Address: 1031 Franklin Street, second floor, San Francisco, CA 94109

entries.title: California homeless birth-certificate fee waiver
entries.description:
A person experiencing homelessness may request a certified California birth record without the normal fee. A qualifying homeless-services provider must complete the affidavit; identity and record requirements still apply.
California Vital Records and fee-waiver forms

entries.title: Homeless Advocacy Project
entries.description:
Phone: 415-575-3130; toll-free 800-405-4427.
Free legal and social-service help for people experiencing or at imminent risk of homelessness, including disability benefits, eviction, SSI and immigration documentation. New-client drop-in is Tuesday–Friday, 1–3 p.m.; closed Mondays.
Official Homeless Advocacy Project page
entries.address: Address: 125 Hyde Street, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: Legal Advice and Referral Clinic at GLIDE
entries.description:
2026 schedule: third Wednesday monthly, 10 a.m.–noon, walk-in. Low-income people receive priority. Volunteer lawyers provide brief civil advice and referrals; representation is not guaranteed.
Official clinic schedule
entries.address: Address: GLIDE Sanctuary, second floor, 330 Ellis Street, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: Immigration legal-help directory
entries.description:
The City lists nonprofit legal providers by language and type of case. Call before visiting; eligibility and case capacity differ. Do not pay a notario or unlicensed adviser for legal representation.
Official San Francisco immigration legal resources

categories.title: Families, young people, survivors, LGBTQ+ people and veterans

entries.title: Domestic violence — immediate safety
entries.description:
Call 911 for immediate danger. For confidential support, call La Casa de las Madres at 877-503-1850 or WOMAN, Inc. at 877-384-3578, both 24 hours.
Confidential shelter addresses are not published. If an abusive person may monitor the device, use a safe telephone if possible.
Official survivor resources

entries.title: Riley Center and Brennan House
entries.description:
24-hour support line: 415-255-0165. St. Vincent de Paul provides confidential survivor support, emergency shelter, transitional housing, case management and advocacy.
Brennan House accepts all genders, including male survivors, and children. Availability requires assessment.
Official domestic-violence services

entries.title: SafeHouse Hope Center
entries.description:
Phone: 415-643-7861. Hours: Monday–Friday, 1–9 p.m.
Drop-in help for women experiencing homelessness and sexual exploitation: food, bathrooms, hygiene, computers and connections to housing, legal and health services. It is not a guaranteed overnight bed.
Official Hope Center page
entries.address: Address: 1089 Mission Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: Larkin Street Youth Services — ages 18–24
entries.description:
24-hour help line: 800-669-6196. Drop-in support includes breakfast, lunch, showers, laundry, rest pods, computers, Wi-Fi, clinic care, counseling, education and employment.
Official drop-in center page
entries.address: Address: 134 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: SF LGBT Center youth services
entries.description:
The Center serves LGBTQ+ young people with drop-in support and acts as a Youth Coordinated Entry access point. Ask about current housing navigation, employment and community services.
Official youth-services page
entries.address: Address: 1800 Market Street, San Francisco, CA 94102

entries.title: Swords to Plowshares Veterans Center
entries.description:
Main phone: 415-252-4788. No-fee case management, benefits and discharge assistance, legal help, employment, counseling and housing navigation. Staff can help obtain ID and DD-214 records.
Drop-ins are accepted for services, but off-site housing is referral-only.
Official veterans-center contact page
entries.address: Address: 1060 Howard Street, San Francisco, CA 94103

entries.title: San Francisco VA Downtown Clinic
entries.description:
New-patient hotline: 415-750-2281. Walk-in medical and social-work services Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Homeless-veteran line: 877-424-3838. Crisis: call 988, then press 1.
Official VA San Francisco resources
entries.address: Address: 401 Third Street, San Francisco, CA 94107

entries.title: Help in other languages and for immigrants
entries.description:
311 provides free language assistance. SFHSA lists benefit-application partners serving Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin and other language communities. Immigration status affects some benefits but not every service; ask a qualified worker.
Official immigrant-service organizations

entries.title: Veterinary Street Outreach Services — Vet SOS
entries.description:
Tell every shelter or access point about an animal before accepting placement. A pet, service animal and emotional-support animal may be treated differently. Do not surrender an animal before asking about a kennel, temporary care, food or veterinary support.
Phone: 415-355-2248. Free twice-monthly pop-up veterinary clinics for unhoused San Francisco pet owners and some recently housed clients.
Wellness exams, vaccines, testing, supplies and referrals for free spay or neuter care. Appointment and eligibility confirmation are required; this is not emergency care.
Official eligibility and appointment instructions

entries.title: Full Belly Bus
entries.description:
Phone: 415-635-1007. Free pet food, veterinary wellness help, grooming and supplies to unhoused people with dogs and cats through mobile events.
The Food 4 Paws page lists recurring distributions. Dates change; call or check before traveling.
Current pet-food locations and resources

entries.title: SF SPCA Community Veterinary Clinic
entries.description:
Text: 415-554-3084. Hours: Wednesday–Saturday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m. — sms:+14155543084
Affordable preventive care and treatment for selected minor conditions. It does not provide emergencies, X-rays, laboratory diagnostics, adoption or health certificates.
Official clinic services and booking
entries.address: Address: 4527 Mission Street, San Francisco, CA 94112

entries.title: Pet-aware shelter options
entries.description:
Lark-Inn publishes a pet kennel for youth ages 18–24. Other shelter rules differ. When calling 628-652-8000 or an access point, state the animal type, size and whether it is a trained service animal.
A kennel or animal-friendly policy does not guarantee a human shelter bed or space for the animal.
Lark-Inn services
